rv.q: The Hungry Ghost as a production simply gets everything right.
She makes an already striking play about the push and pull between cultural tradition and independence all the more compelling.
For a first-time playwright, The Hungry Ghost is a confident and wonderfully original piece of writing, and one that leaves its audience hungry for whatever Yew serves up next.
It's enjoyable and worth seeing – expect to laugh a lot – but it isn't flawless.
It’s warm, hilariously funny and heartfelt.
Everything about The Hungry Ghost feels exciting.
The Ghost's departure from Girl leaves a sense of a story well rounded and well told, though a little more time with the Ghost's life before she became a ghost might have been even more satisfying.
The Hungry Ghost is a true example of why to go to the theatre: with its unique story and excellent production, its compelling from start to finish and leaves you hungry for more.

cn.t: Mei Leng Yew's debut earns widespread acclaim for its sharp writing and hilarious set pieces. Critics praise Mei Mac's outstanding performance and the play's skillful blend of Chinese folklore with heartfelt exploration of identity and family expectations.
